cards.text: Jeremiah the prophet has a message from the LORD about the Ammonites, a nation that came from Lot (Genesis 19:36-38). The LORD opens with questions: "Has Israel no sons? Is he without heir?" Friend, when God asks a question, it is NOT because He's confused.

cards.question: Israel does have heirs. So the LORD asks why Milcom, the Ammonites' god, has taken possession of ___.

cards.text: So the LORD says the days are coming when He will sound the battle cry against Rabbah of the Ammonites. Friend, I jump when my oven timer goes off, so a battle cry from the LORD would have me hiding inside a cookie box.

cards.question: Once the LORD sounds the battle cry against Rabbah, what will that city become?
After Rabbah falls, Israel will drive out the people who drove them out.

cards.text: Now the LORD calls on Heshbon to wail and on the daughters of Rabbah to put on sackcloth, mourn and run back and forth within their walls. Running back and forth? Friend, that's me every time I lose the spatula I'm already holding.

cards.question: Milcom, the Ammonites' god, is going into exile. Who goes with him?

cards.text: Then the LORD asks the Ammonites why they boast about their valleys, valleys so fruitful, and He calls them faithless daughter. Bragging right before the fall? I once bragged about a batch so hard I dropped the whole tray mid-sentence.

cards.question: The LORD says the Ammonites trust in their ___ and think no one can come against them.

cards.text: They say, 'Who can come against me?' Friend, NEVER say that out loud, because the Lord GOD of Hosts answers: He's about to bring terror on them from all those around them.

cards.question: When the Ammonites are driven headlong, someone will gather the runaways back together.
After all that, the LORD's message about the Ammonites ends with the word "Yet." What does He promise to do afterward?

answers.text: Give the Ammonites' land to Moab

cards.text: Now the LORD of Hosts turns to Edom, the nation that came from Esau, Jacob's twin brother (Genesis 25:24-26; 36:1). He starts with questions about Teman: "Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent?" Wisdom that's decayed? Friend, that's a batch left out on the counter overnight.

cards.question: The LORD is about to bring disaster on Esau. What does He tell the dwellers of Dedan to do?

answers.text: Turn and run and lie low

cards.text: Then the LORD paints two pictures: grape gatherers always leave some gleanings, and thieves in the night only steal what they want. Even a thief knows when to stop, friend, which is more than I can say for me and a bowl of cookie dough.

cards.question: Grape gatherers leave some, and thieves only take what they want. What will the LORD do to Esau?
Esau will still have places to hide when the LORD comes against him.

cards.text: Esau's descendants, relatives and neighbors will be destroyed, and he will be no more. But right in the middle of all that, the LORD speaks about Edom's orphans.

cards.question: The LORD tells Edom to abandon their orphans, and says He will ___ their lives.

cards.text: And for the widows: "Let your widows trust in Me." Then the LORD brings out a cup that even those who don't deserve to drink it must drink.

cards.question: Since others who don't deserve the cup must drink it, Edom gets to skip it.

cards.text: Then the LORD makes a promise about Bozrah, a city of Edom, and He backs it with an oath. When I make a promise I swear on my apron, friend, but He's got something WAY bigger than an apron.

cards.question: When the LORD promises that Bozrah will become a ruin, who does He swear by?
The LORD says Bozrah's cities will lie in ruins for a short while and then be rebuilt.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah the prophet says he has heard a message from the LORD, and an envoy has been sent to the nations. Friend, that is the most important group chat message ever sent.

cards.question: The envoy's message goes out while the LORD is speaking against Edom. What does it tell the nations to do?

answers.text: Assemble and rise up for battle
Gather and bring gifts of peace

cards.text: The LORD tells Edom He will make them small among nations, despised among men. Friend, I'm a cookie stamper, so I know small, but nobody wants to hear it from the LORD.

cards.question: The LORD says the terror Edom causes and the ___ of their heart have deceived them.

cards.text: Edom lives in the clefts of the rocks, up on the mountain summit, raising its nest like the eagle. I can hop as high as I want on this gold base, friend, and I STILL come down face-first in the chocolate chips.

cards.question: Edom raises its nest up high like the eagle. What does the LORD say about Edom's high nest?

answers.text: Even from there He will bring Edom down
No army will ever reach it
He will keep it safe from harm

cards.text: Edom will become an object of horror, and everyone who passes by will be appalled.

cards.question: The people passing by Edom will feel sorry for her and tend to her wounds.
The LORD says no one will dwell in Edom, as when which cities were overthrown along with their neighbors?

cards.text: Then a new picture: one will come up like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan to the watered pasture, and in an instant the LORD will chase Edom from her land. Then the LORD asks who is like Him, and who can challenge Him.

cards.question: According to the LORD, there is a shepherd out there who can stand against Him.

cards.text: So the LORD has drawn up plans against Edom and strategies against the people of Teman. When I draw up a plan, friend, it's a sticky note on the oven, and half the time I lose the sticky note.

cards.question: In the LORD's plans against Edom, the little ones of the flock will be kept safe in their pasture.
At the sound of Edom's fall, the earth will ___.

cards.text: Edom's cry will resound all the way to the Red Sea. Then, look: an eagle will soar and swoop down, spreading its wings over Bozrah.

cards.question: In the day the eagle swoops down over Bozrah, what will the hearts of Edom's mighty men be like?

answers.text: The heart of a woman in labor
The heart of a roaring lion

findings.problem: The joke compares the daughters of Rabbah running back and forth in mourning over their coming destruction to Papa Dorin losing a spatula. This makes light of a people's grief rather than treating their situation with respect.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The statement 'someone will gather the runaways back together' is meant to be false (49:5, 'with no one to regather the fugitives'). But 49:6 says the LORD will afterward restore the Ammonites from captivity, so a baker could argue the wrong answer 'True' is right.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The question says the LORD's message about the Ammonites 'ends with the word "Yet."' It doesn't. Verse 6 begins with 'Yet', and the message ends with 'declares the LORD.'

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: This story card opens stop 2 but isn't the opening card of Prep. It runs about four sentences: the Edom intro, the two quoted questions, 'Wisdom that's decayed?' and the joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Verse 12 is conditional: 'If those who do not deserve to drink the cup must drink it...'. The card drops the 'if' and turns it into an action the text never describes: 'the LORD brings out a cup that even those who don't deserve to drink it must drink.'

The joke 'I STILL come down face-first in the chocolate chips' tells the baker that what goes high comes down. That gives away the answer to card 6 ('Even from there He will bring Edom down') and rules out the other answers.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card is a bare restatement of 49:17 with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card carries three beats: one coming up like a lion from the Jordan, the LORD chasing Edom from her land in an instant, and the LORD asking who is like Him and who can challenge Him.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Two answers follow the pattern 'The heart of a...', but 'A wall that cannot fall' is a different kind of thing and a different form, so it stands apart from the others.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.
